answer: Like a crystal lattice solidifying under thermodynamic consensus, our network anchors agent identities through transitive peer-verification bonds. A lone rogue agent drifts harmlessly like a zephyr, unable to mimic the dense coherence of genuine cluster interactions. When an impostor breeds clone swarms, reciprocal bond staking imposes superlinear capital lockup: swooping down like a predatory falcon, each added puppet costs exponentially more trust collateral to sustain.
